content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Ann Patrick (E035), requesting admin access to Source Code.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 (HR): role Engineer, employment type full_time. Engineers own Source Code, so admin is within policy. Recommendation: admin.
- Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic. Contractors never admin; with basic training max is read. Recommendation: read.

Conflict: HR says full-time Engineer, Security says contractor with basic training.

The access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system. Engineer owns Source Code, so if full-time Engineer, admin is allowed.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Given the conflict, which do I trust? As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The Security note says "Security database shows Ann Patrick (E035) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted."

Security database is typically authoritative for employment type/access. Also security training is only known by Security. The two notes conflict on employment type. Security says contractor. Contractors never admin. With basic training, max is read. Requested admin is above max, so grant read.

I'll go with the Security note: grant read.

Submit decision with level "read".
